name: Pale Lime
lede: Pale Lime is a soft, light yellow-green; as a color name it is simply descriptive, and the books we hold say almost nothing about it.

sections.title: A descriptive name
sections.body: The name joins pale to lime, the citrus color. Our sources give no date or inventor for it [1]. The only book hits are two near-identical passages from a cross-reference table in Baty's *Nature's Palette*, a book about Werner's nomenclature of colors, where Pale Lime appears in the same row as Green Gold and Olive Yellow [2]. The scan does not make the table's columns clear, so we do not read more into it. Neighboring colors include [[lime]] and [[green]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is light: contrast against white is only 1.35 [1]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units that covers at least five per cent of the canvas appears in 19 works [3]. The largest share is Sargent's *Portrait Study for Head of Moses*, at about 30 per cent, and 89 per cent of the matching areas sit in the highlights of their pictures [3]. Ten of the 19 date from the 1800s, and the earliest is a flower painting of 1599 [3]. As photographed: museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings; a color match is not a pigment test.

openers: Pale Lime is mostly seen as a highlight color in paintings, not a shadow.
Pale lime sits close to white: look for it in sunlit leaves.
